name: Brixlegg
kurzbeschreibung: Historic market town in the Inntal with its Silberbergwerk, Schloss Matzen, and late Gothic parish church.
beschreibung:
Overview

Brixlegg is a historic market town in the Lower Inn Valley in Tyrol's Kufstein district, situated at an altitude of approximately 534 meters where the Alpbacher Ache stream flows into the Inn River. Home to around 3,100 residents, the vibrant town serves as the historic gateway to the Alpbach Valley. Bordering Rattenberg, Austria's smallest town, and Kramsach, Brixlegg occupies a central hub in the Tyrolean lowlands. The community bridges thousands of years of metallurgical heritage with tranquil recreational nature: it hosts Austria's sole copper smelter alongside the grand, romantic landscape gardens of Matzen Park.

History

Human settlement here is inextricably linked to metallurgy, as copper ores were mined and smelted in the surrounding mountains as early as the Bronze Age over 3,500 years ago. The village was first documented in 788 in the Indiculus Arnonis records as Prisslech. In 1463, Duke Ludwig the Rich of Bavaria founded the central smelting works in Brixlegg to process silver and copper ores mined in Schwaz, Kitzbühel, and Rattenberg. This gave rise to Montanwerke Brixlegg, which established one of the world's earliest electrolytic copper refineries in 1885 and remains an international leader in recycled secondary copper production today. The parish church of the Nuptials of Our Lady was built between 1508 and 1520 as a Late Gothic miners' church backed by Emperor Maximilian I, later receiving a lavish Baroque interior in 1768. The medieval fortress Schloss Matzen, once held by the Fugger dynasty, stands as a grand testament to the town's mining fortunes.

How to Get There

By car, Brixlegg is reached via the Inntal motorway A12, exiting at Kramsach/Brixlegg/Alpbachtal, or toll-free from Bavaria along federal road B171. Rail passengers benefit from excellent connections: Brixlegg railway station on the Lower Inn Valley line is served every 30 minutes by Tyrolean S-Bahn lines S4 and S8 as well as regional REX express trains. The station forecourt serves as the main bus interchange into the Alpbach Valley and Kramsach.

Tips

A crowning highlight is Matzen Park (Schlosspark Matzen), an English landscape garden spanning 200,000 square meters featuring ancient exotic trees, tranquil ponds, and the fairytale castle of Schloss Matzen. The Tyrolean Mining and Smelting Museum Brixlegg showcases six thousand years of regional mining history through authentic mine carts and historic tools. Visitors can easily walk across to the medieval glassblowing town of Rattenberg or hike into the scenic Kundler Klamm gorge. In summer, the nearby Kramsach lakes on the opposite bank of the Inn invite guests to swim and relax.
